questions.question: What does a Mono represent in WebClient?
options: A list that always has many items
Zero or one value that arrives in the future
questions.explanation: A Mono is a container for at most one value that will be available later, while a Flux can hold many.

questions.question: Which starter gives a Boot 4 project the WebClient class without adding a WebFlux server?
questions.explanation: spring-boot-starter-webclient brings WebClient and its auto-configuration, and it works beside the web starter.

questions.question: In the CineGo code, Monsoon Express has 4.3 stars and The Silent Orbit has 3.9. What does the compare endpoint return for those two?
options: The Silent Orbit 3.9 vs Monsoon Express 4.3
Monsoon Express 4.3 vs The Silent Orbit 3.9
questions.explanation: Mono.zip keeps the order of the two calls, so the first movie comes first in the text.

questions.question: The safe-rating endpoint has a one second timeout and onErrorReturn. The rating service takes three seconds. What does the caller get?
options: The real rating after three seconds
Rating not available right now after about one second
An empty reply with no text
questions.explanation: The timeout fires after one second, and onErrorReturn replaces the error with the fallback text.

questions.question: A developer builds a WebClient chain with get, uri, retrieve and bodyToMono, but never calls block or subscribe. What happens?
options: The request is sent and the result is ignored
Spring throws an exception at startup
questions.explanation: A Mono is lazy, so nothing runs until something subscribes to it, for example block().
